policy: The entire previously observed specialist calibration/evaluation pool of 384 questions becomes development. Rank its 12 titles by SHA256(str(seed)+title), allocate the first 8 articles (256 questions) to train and the remaining 4 (128 questions) to calibration. Preserve every original field except split. For new evaluation, cumulatively exclude all prior inventoried titles/IDs/normalized exact contexts/questions plus all 384 specialist rows; select four remaining eligible articles with the unchanged hash-rank selector and 4000-character limit. Require 16 unique contexts in each answerability class per article. No quota relaxation, seed search, output-based sample replacement, or new model inference in the selector.

scope: One additional supervised correctness-ranking hypothesis, after the frozen specialist policy failed public-benchmark evaluation. All old specialist 384 rows, including failed evaluation, are explicitly development and cannot support a new holdout claim. The new 128-row evaluation is a fixed local public SQuAD2 benchmark assessment, not model-unseen confirmation or official hidden test: the upstream specialist was trained on SQuAD2 and already publicly evaluated on dev. Article-level disjointness and exact filtering do not remove upstream benchmark exposure, pretraining contamination, semantic near-duplicates, or the sequence of project-level hypothesis decisions. Only four remaining articles limit external validity. If this one fixed hypothesis fails, retain failure and stop further model/feature search in this round.
